votes.headline: Approved a non-binding deal to pursue a new Rays ballpark in Tampa
votes.inShort: The commission approved a non-binding memorandum of understanding with the Tampa Bay Rays and the City of Tampa for a ballpark and mixed-use district on Hillsborough College's Dale Mabry campus. It set the terms the final contracts would follow.

facts.text: Clerk's record: roll call sheet 5486, agenda item B-1.
Total project cost estimated at about $2.3 billion.
County share up to $796 million: $360 million Community Investment Tax, more than $260 million tourist tax bonds, $103 million other county funds.

votes.headline: Gave final approval to county funding for a new Rays ballpark
votes.inShort: At a special meeting, the commission approved the development and funding agreement, guaranty and team non-relocation agreement for a Rays ballpark on Hillsborough College's Dale Mabry campus. The county's share is capped at $796 million, and the Rays cover more than $1.3 billion plus cost overruns.

facts.text: County funding cap: $796 million ($360 million Community Investment Tax, $263 million tourist development tax, $103 million other funds, $30 million federal disaster-recovery money).
The Rays pay more than $1.3 billion plus all cost overruns.
Tampa City Council approved its part 4 to 3 the day before.
Still pending after this vote: ballpark license and use agreement, community benefits agreement, construction funds trust agreement.
The Clerk's 2026 voting record PDF (printed Oct 9, 2026) ends Aug 13, 2026, so it does not yet show this roll call.

votes.dateNote: FOX 13 reported a 4-3 approval on Oct 7, 2026; Bay News 9 reported a 4-3 final approval on Oct 21, 2026.
votes.headline: Approved $75 million for ZooTampa renovations and expansion
votes.inShort: The county will pay ZooTampa $5 million a year through 2041 from Community Investment Tax (half-cent sales tax) money, and the zoo must match it, for $150 million in upgrades and a new South America section. Some commissioners argued the money should be shared with other cultural groups.

facts.text: County money: $75 million, $5 million a year through 2041, matched 1 to 1 by the zoo.
On Sept 16, 2026 a majority voted to have staff finalize the partnership.

votes.headline: Approved changes to the proposed FY 2027 budget
votes.inShort: At a budget reconciliation hearing on a recommended $14.1 billion FY 2027 budget, commissioners voted on items they had flagged for change. The plan included a millage swap to support public safety and other county services.

facts.text: Final FY 2027 tax rates and the final budget vote.
